stories.headline: Nemotron 3.5-Parse gets speed boost
stories.body: **Open data, faster inference:** HuggingFace details new fine‑tuning tricks and data releases that shave latency on the Nemotron 3.5‑Parse model. Engineers can now iterate quicker without sacrificing quality.
stories.why: Speedier loops mean more experiments per day for model developers.

stories.headline: Routeability audit shows little headroom
stories.body: **Benchmarks, limited gains:** The RAP framework and RouteabilityBench ran 66 LLMs across four routing tests and found only marginal improvements on coarse scores. The ceiling is lower than hoped.
stories.why: Helps teams avoid wasted tuning on routing when gains are minimal.

stories.headline: Linux driver‑taint patch reverted
stories.body: **Patch backtrack:** A Linux 7.4 change that marked the kernel tainted after manual driver bind/unbind was rolled back after breaking real‑world workflows. The kernel stays clean for now.
stories.why: Prevents unnecessary panic for developers debugging driver issues.

highlights.title: Building on Nemotron 3.5 Parse: Open Data, Fine-Tuning, and Faster Inference
highlights.summary: The HuggingFace blog details open data, fine‑tuning methods, and inference speed improvements for the Nemotron 3.5‑Parse model.
highlights.detail: The post explains how publicly available datasets are leveraged to fine‑tune Nemotron 3.5‑Parse, and describes engineering changes that reduce latency during generation. It also compares the new inference pipeline to the original baseline, noting modest throughput gains without sacrificing quality.

highlights.title: Routeability Before Routing: Routeability Audit Protocol (RAP) and RouteabilityBench for Audited LLM Model Selection
highlights.summary: The Routeability Audit Protocol (RAP) and RouteabilityBench evaluate LLM routing on four benchmarks covering 66 models, revealing limited room for improvement on coarse‑scored tests.
highlights.detail: RAP runs after a benchmark‑portfolio score matrix exists, auditing whether routing decisions are meaningful before comparing routers. It highlights that many models tie on coarse metrics, making routing gains hard to certify. The package is released as a runnable claim‑verification tool.

highlights.title: Can image generation help visual reasoning? An empirical study
highlights.summary: Adding generated helper images reduces mean accuracy of vision‑language models by 3.7 percentage points, with a 10.47‑point drop on VSTAR and a 3‑point gain only on ERQA after ten edits.
highlights.detail: The study paired 13 vision‑language models with image generators, letting the model request a helper image before answering. Most tasks saw performance declines, and two unified models (BAGEL, Janus‑Pro‑7B) lost accuracy on eight tasks each. Only ERQA showed modest improvement after extensive image editing.

highlights.title: Make the Adversary Spend More: Stateful Deception as a Cost-Exchange Primitive for AI-Era Cyber Defense
highlights.summary: The paper proposes stateful deception for cyber defense, using persistent adversary‑specific state to increase attacker effort while limiting defender compute.
highlights.detail: Instead of resetting honeypots, each recognized adversary is placed in a coherent simulated environment that reflects its prior actions, isolated from others. The language model only renders explicit state, never stores it, and the authors define a Deception Exchange Rate (DER) to quantify the cost trade‑off. An SSH honeypot built on Cowrie demonstrates the concept.

highlights.title: [$] Tainting (or not) on manual driver binding
highlights.summary: A Linux 7.4 patch that marked the kernel tainted when users manually bind or unbind drivers was reverted after causing real‑world workflow issues.
highlights.detail: The change was intended to filter out fuzz‑generated bug reports, but it also interfered with legitimate debugging and testing scenarios. Its reversal highlights the need for more nuanced kernel interfaces for driver management.

items.title: Where scientists draw the line on AI agents
items.summary: The HuggingFace blog surveys where scientists draw ethical and practical boundaries on AI agents.
items.detail: The article compiles viewpoints from researchers about acceptable uses, risk thresholds, and regulatory considerations for autonomous AI systems. It highlights divergent opinions on agency, accountability, and the role of human oversight, providing a snapshot of current community consensus.

items.title: Model: inclusionAI/LingSante-3.1-flash
items.summary: The inclusionAI/LingSante‑3.1‑flash model has been downloaded 1,487 times and received 198 likes on HuggingFace.
items.detail: This text‑generation model, listed among trending HF models, targets French medical language tasks. Its popularity reflects community interest in domain‑specific LLMs, and the like count suggests positive reception among early adopters.

items.title: Model: nvidia/Nemotron-Labs-Image-30B-A3B
items.summary: Nvidia Nemotron Labs released a 30B‑parameter text‑to‑image model on Hugging Face, currently showing 218 downloads and 212 likes.
items.detail: The model is part of the Nemotron series aimed at high‑quality image generation from prompts. Its modest download count suggests early adoption, and the like count indicates community interest. It is available under the standard HF model license.

items.title: Model: prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2.5-27B-GGUF
items.summary: Prism‑ML published a 27B‑parameter ternary Bonsai model in GGUF format, reaching 59,366 downloads and 421 likes on Hugging Face.
items.detail: The GGUF binary format targets efficient inference on consumer‑grade hardware. The ternary quantization reduces memory use while preserving performance, making it attractive for text‑generation workloads on edge devices.

items.title: Daisy Chaining Stepper Motors
items.summary: Hackaday outlines approaches to control many stepper motors, from multi‑channel driver boards to custom microcontroller solutions.
items.detail: The guide compares off‑the‑shelf controllers with DIY designs, discussing trade‑offs in wiring complexity, power distribution, and firmware flexibility. It also offers wiring diagrams and code snippets for common microcontrollers.

items.title: Dave Täht given the Jonathan B. Postel Service Award
items.summary: Dave Täht was awarded the Jonathan B. Postel Service Award for his work on bufferbloat mitigation, global connectivity, and mentoring.
items.detail: Täht’s contributions include early research on latency in broadband networks, deployment of community hubs in Nicaragua, and collaboration with projects like Starlink to reduce latency. The award recognizes his lasting impact on Internet performance.

items.title: Pop!_OS 26.04 LTS released
items.summary: System76 released Pop!_OS 26.04 LTS, built on Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, adding tablet support and new COSMIC applications.
items.detail: The LTS release promises five years of updates and introduces automatic system updates, enhanced drawing tablet integration, and a suite of refreshed COSMIC desktop tools. Existing Pop!_OS 24.04 LTS users will receive the upgrade starting December.

items.title: Security updates for Wednesday
items.summary: Security updates were released on Wednesday for AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, and Oracle Linux, covering dozens of packages including emacs, Go toolsets, Xwayland, flatpak, Chromium, MariaDB, .NET runtimes, and OpenSSH.
items.detail: Each distribution listed specific affected components, ranging from core system libraries to high-level applications. The updates address vulnerabilities disclosed in recent advisories, requiring administrators to apply them promptly to maintain system integrity. No single package count is provided, but the breadth spans multiple language runtimes, database connectors, and container tools.

items.detail: Libtt brings the PyTorch and JAX ecosystem to Tenstorrent hardware. It implements PJRT, the interface through which XLA-based frameworks drive Google's TPUs, so JAX runs on it directly, PyTorch runs through TorchTPU, and software written for TPUs carries over with no changes except replacing custom kernels. items.title: Single-Database Rewards Are Hackable: Counterfactual Execution for Trustworthy Text-to-SQL RL
items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) for text-to-SQL agents pays a query when its result matches the reference on one database. However, a wrong query can match by luck when the data lack the rows that expose its bug. We study a …
items.detail: Reinforcement learning (RL) for text-to-SQL agents pays a query when its result matches the reference on one database. However, a wrong query can match by luck when the data lack the rows that expose its bug. We study a counterfactual-database (CF) reward that also runs the final query on a few hidden, code-generated copies of the database and pays only if all results match (strict form) or by the share matched (mean form). items.title: PipeAxes: Decoupling Compute and Communication Granularities for Pipeline-Parallel LLM Serving
items.summary: PipeAxes decouples compute and communication granularity for pipeline-parallel LLM serving, running wide prefill batches a few layers at a time and achieving latency targets for all 74 requests in a ten‑fold bandwidth test.
items.detail: The system slices prefill batches so decodes can interleave, using a fused Triton Hadamard‑INT4 codec to compress activations sent in variable‑sized row groups over TCP. The scheduler picks batch width, slice depth, and row‑group size based on latency slack, reducing weight reloads and link idle time.

items.title: An Efficient and Uniform CSP Solution Generator Generator
items.summary: The paper introduces a specialized solving method with a dedicated propagation scheme to generate uniform, efficient random generators for CSP solution spaces.
items.detail: By producing a representation suited for random sampling, the approach simplifies the creation of input generators that respect complex constraints, improving the practicality of constraint‑based random testing for functional verification.

items.title: wealthfolio/wealthfolio
items.summary: Wealthfolio is a Rust‑based, private, local‑first personal finance tracker covering investments, net worth, spending, and simulations.
items.detail: Designed for offline use, the tool stores data locally without cloud dependencies, offering a secure way to manage financial information and run scenario analyses.

items.title: zhouxiaoka/autoclip
items.summary: AutoClip is an open‑source AI video clipping desktop tool that converts long videos into short, platform‑ready clips with subtitles, cover images, and posting copy.
items.detail: It supports automatic generation of content for TikTok, YouTube Shorts, Reels, and other short‑form platforms, streamlining repurposing of podcasts, interviews, and courses.
